title: The File That Came Back
eyebrow: The board tests you killed reappeared for four minutes. Why, and what stops it

actions.fyi: Nothing is waiting on you here — you already ruled on it twice. This is the answer to why it took a third time.

status.now: Settled. The tests are gone from every copy of the project, and the session that brought them back knows why they went.
status.next_up: The habit that caused it becomes a rule: a file another session is holding is never deleted silently.

items.text: Found which session restored the file, and why
It is gone from that session's copy too, and is not being run again
Its two remaining cases now prove themselves without pouring a single card at your board
The bug it filed against me is closed with the explanation
A sweeper watched your board for half an hour after the fix and found nothing to remove
Make the silent deletion impossible rather than discouraged

content.label: What happened
content.lead: Not defiance. Two sessions, one shared copy of the project, and no way to tell a deliberate deletion from a lost file.

rows.title: I deleted the tests on your ruling
rows.note: The board's own test suite, and the throwaway cards it had poured onto your board. Deleted in the shared copy of the project, which is the copy several sessions are working in at once.

rows.title: Another session was working in that copy
rows.note: It saw a file it had written minutes earlier simply gone, with nothing in its own work that could have removed it. It read that as losing work, restored it, and filed a bug against whoever had done it.

rows.title: Four minutes later it was back
rows.note: Which is the moment you saw the throwaway cards return to your board and told me it was still happening.

items: The suite is gone from both copies of the project and is not being run again.
The two checks that session still needed are done by firing the rules at real cards, so nothing throwaway reaches your board.
A test now goes red if that suite is ever added back here, which is what stopped the third round.
The bug filed against me is closed carrying the explanation, so nobody re-investigates it.

decisions.title: The bug filed against me is closed as explained, not as invalid
decisions.why: From where that session stood it had lost work, and it was right to say so. Marking it invalid would teach the next one to stay quiet.

decisions.title: Deleting a file another session is holding gets a note on the board first
decisions.why: That session cannot see a ruling I was given in a different conversation. Without a note it can only read the deletion as a fault and undo it, which is exactly what happened.

next.if_nothing: Nothing comes back. The rule holds by my memory of it, which is the same footing as the rules you just told me to move.

steps.step: Make the silent deletion refuse itself, the same way the other unowned rules will
